english: Shepherd, three of my goats are missing (have been left). Did you sell them earlier? Master, I did not sell them. A wolf seized them; I saw their blood on the stone. And where were you? I was driving the other goats to water. Will you show me the wolf's tracks? I show them to you. Will you go there now? I go. If the tracks are there, you owe me nothing.
uncertain: lelikʷḗr: 'have been left' read as 'are missing'
pédās vs pédeh₂es: two different stems for 'tracks'

english: Master, summer has passed; give me my wage. What shall I say to you? Say it: I owe(?) you a foal and a lamb. On the mountain a wolf snatched the lamb, and all summer I worked for you. You speak boldly, orphan. Take the foal and leave the lamb to me. Give me that too, or I go to the king. Now take it, boldly.
uncertain: sékʷs moy ... could be 'you tell me'

english: Do you hear that? Someone is in the cowshed. I hear. Be quiet. Do you see? A young man is leading a foal out of the cowshed. Shall we follow him? He is taking a spear; let us follow him. At dawn we will tell the elders what we have seen. Will they believe us? They will believe us, because we speak the truth.
uncertain: bʰebʰidʰḗr read as perfect of bʰeydʰ 'trust' rather than fear

english: Famous king, (the king) drove me out of the village. Why did the king drive you out? I killed an enemy in battle. He came against me with a spear. Did no one see it? No one saw it, and the king hated me. He hated his kinship(?). Where shall we go, dear? We go to my grandfather. Now I will follow you, and our children will follow too.

What, grandfather, is an oath? An oath is a mortal's word to the gods, which he speaks. They hear it and remember it. What do they do to men who lie? They punish him. His cattle perish and his sons are few. Child, will you lie to your father? Grandfather, I do not lie to him. I fear the gods. Now Dyeus gives you a long life.

Mother-in-law, my husband's sister took my wool. Why did she take it? She says: 'I spun it.' Which of you two spun it? I spun it, and my brother's wife saw me. Now I will ask her. If she still says that, your sister-in-law will give it back to you. And will she be angry with me? Let her be angry; she (you?) speaks the truth.
